content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through setting up the jquery development environment with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns preparing an html, css, and javascript project into a repeatable implementation choice. A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates setting up the jquery development environment using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in setting up the jquery development environment.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: The page loads the pinned jQuery library and then the app script in dependency order.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Setting Up the jQuery Development Environment is one part of the installation and development environment workflow.
A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.
Use the official API or upgrade guide for version-specific behavior and verify an example locally before relying on it.
